title: Exact functor action on finite filtered objects
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories and $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ additive and exact. Fix either no common filtration interval, or an interval $(a,b)$. For finite filtered objects and their evaluations [def-trf-finite-filtered-localization, def-trf-filtered-operation-lift-structures], there exists an additive functor $H_F$ between these categories and natural isomorphisms $H_F\circ E_p\cong E_p\circ H$ for every total or graded evaluation $p$. Each filtration step of $H_F(K)$ is canonically isomorphic to $H(F^pK)$, and this isomorphism identifies its inclusion followed by the underlying-object comparison with $H$ of the original step inclusion. This is an assertion about filtered objects only, with no homotopy category or localization conclusion.

Canonical operation/adjunction lifts: literature/varshavsky-lefschetz-verdier-trace-formula_arXiv-math0505564.pdf, Lemma 5.1.4 and §§5.2.1–5.2.2; the pro-etale compactification-relative formulation is assembled from the same filtered-injective construction.

proof.text: Send a filtration step to the monomorphism H of its inclusion. Exactness preserves monomorphisms, zero objects, and cokernels. Represent these monomorphisms by subobjects; use their underlying isomorphisms for the step comparisons. Apply H to all restriction squares to define maps. The cokernel universal property gives the natural graded comparisons. The identity underlying-object comparison and the defining subobject equations give the inclusion equation. The finite and fixed bounds hold because H preserves isomorphisms and zero objects.
